architecture_patterns.name: Edge reverse proxy
architecture_patterns.description: Clients connect to nginx, which terminates or handles HTTP-level traffic and forwards requests to upstream application services.
architecture_patterns.source_basis: Core reverse-proxy role is explicit; detailed deployment flow is a generalized architecture interpretation.

architecture_patterns.name: Static content delivery
architecture_patterns.description: nginx serves static files, index files and optionally auto-indexed directory listings.

architecture_patterns.name: Load-balanced application
architecture_patterns.description: nginx distributes incoming requests across backend servers and can use in-band health checks.
architecture_patterns.source_basis: Load balancing and in-band health checks are explicitly listed.

architecture_patterns.name: Reverse proxy with HTTP caching
architecture_patterns.description: nginx caches eligible responses so repeated requests can be served without always querying the backend.
architecture_patterns.source_basis: Caching is explicit; exact cache policy and bypass rules are not covered in the supplied article.

architecture_patterns.name: Dynamic application integration
architecture_patterns.description: nginx serves as a front end for dynamic content through FastCGI, SCGI, uWSGI, WSGI application servers or Phusion Passenger.

architecture_patterns.name: TLS-enabled frontend
architecture_patterns.description: nginx supports TLS/SSL features such as SNI, OCSP stapling and TLS protocol integrations; a frontend TLS termination topology is a common inference.
architecture_patterns.source_basis: TLS/SSL features are explicit; exact termination topology is inferred.

architecture_patterns.name: Mail protocol proxy
architecture_patterns.description: nginx can proxy SMTP, POP3 and IMAP, with TLS/SSL and STARTTLS; authentication is delegated to an external HTTP server or script.
architecture_patterns.source_basis: Protocol and authentication features are explicit.

architecture_patterns.name: Graceful configuration or executable upgrade
architecture_patterns.description: The article states nginx can upgrade its executable and configuration without losing client connections.
architecture_patterns.source_basis: Explicitly listed feature; operational procedure is not detailed in the supplied article.

architecture_patterns.name: Containerized web frontend
architecture_patterns.description: nginx is commonly deployed in Docker containers according to a 2018 usage survey; container orchestration details are outside the source.
architecture_patterns.source_basis: The source reports a historical survey finding, not a current universal deployment statistic.

architecture_patterns.name: Commercial API gateway and management
architecture_patterns.description: NGINX Plus API gateway functionality was associated with NGINX Controller, announced as an API management tool in 2017.
architecture_patterns.source_basis: Commercial product relationship is explicit; flow is conceptual.

derived_rules.rule: For high numbers of concurrent connections, nginx's asynchronous event-driven approach is a core architectural choice.
derived_rules.rationale: The article contrasts its event-driven model with thread-based handling and connects it to predictable performance under high load.

derived_rules.rule: Do not assume nginx natively supports Apache-style .htaccess per-file overrides.
derived_rules.rationale: The article explicitly identifies this as a flexibility difference.

derived_rules.rule: Verify third-party module compatibility and build requirements before deploying modules.
derived_rules.rationale: The article notes modules may need to be compiled alongside nginx, may not all support dynamic loading, and some still require static linking.

derived_rules.rule: Treat the article's HTTP/3 status as experimental from nginx 1.25.0, not as a blanket statement about every build or later release.
derived_rules.rationale: The source specifically characterizes HTTP/3 as experimental starting with version 1.25.0.

derived_rules.rule: Encrypted Client Hello support depends on using a compatible OpenSSL branch and the relevant nginx build/configuration.
derived_rules.rationale: The source conditions ECH support on nginx 1.29.4 and an OpenSSL branch implementing ECH.

derived_rules.rule: Plan an external HTTP service or authentication script for nginx mail-proxy authentication.
derived_rules.rationale: The source says mail proxy authentication requires an external HTTP server or script.

derived_rules.rule: Do not assume NGINX Unit receives upstream maintenance after October 2025.
derived_rules.rationale: The article says it was archived by maintainers and is no longer receiving updates.

derived_rules.rule: Distinguish the BSD-licensed nginx project from proprietary NGINX Plus.
derived_rules.rationale: The source lists different license models.

derived_rules.rule: When relying on native ACME automation, verify the deployed nginx version and certificate lifecycle configuration.
derived_rules.rationale: The article reports native ACME issuance and renewal support, but does not provide a complete configuration procedure.

derived_rules.rule: Keep popularity figures tied to the survey and date rather than treating them as timeless market share.
